Key differentiating factors include wind speed and direction (stronger westerlies enhance cooling via upwelling), the depth and persistence of low-level stratus, and subtle differences in daytime solar heating before afternoon sea breezes arrive. Historical June averages hover around 66–70°F, so any departure above that range reflects modest marine-layer suppression rather than a full heat event. With resolution based on the official daily maximum (typically from KSFO or equivalent stations), traders are weighting the most recent model runs and NWS updates, which show limited upside beyond the mid-70s but enough uncertainty in boundary-layer mixing to support the tight clustering around 74–77°F.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast model ensembles for Tel Aviv on June 14 show maximum temperatures clustered near 28–29°C, producing nearly even market-implied odds.** Official guidance from the Israel Meteorological Service and global models such as ECMWF and GFS indicate a typical early-summer pattern under subtropical high pressure, with clear to partly cloudy skies, light winds, and minimal cloud cover allowing strong daytime heating. Ensemble spreads remain modest because of stable synoptic conditions, yet small differences in boundary-layer moisture, sea-breeze timing, or afternoon mixing can shift the daily peak by 1°C. Historical June climatology places average highs near 29–31°C, so current guidance sits slightly below normal. Traders are therefore pricing the narrow window between 28°C and 29°C highest while assigning low probability to outliers, reflecting both model consensus and the inherent uncertainty range of short-range temperature forecasts.

**Trader sentiment for Wellington's highest temperature on June 15, 2026, clusters around 16–17°C because short-range forecasts from MetService and other models indicate a northwesterly flow that favors modest warming above the June climatological mean of ~13°C.** Persistent northwesterlies, potentially strengthened by a foehn effect across the North Island ranges, are expected to deliver daytime highs near 15–16°C, with some guidance edging toward 16°C under clearer or drier conditions before rain arrives later in the day. Southwesterly shifts in the evening could cap further warming and introduce cooler maritime air.

Key differentiating factors include exact timing of the wind shift, cloud cover, and whether any foehn warming fully develops—elements that produce the tight 16°C vs. 17°C split. Recent model runs show limited spread, but small adjustments in steering flow or insolation could easily tip the daily maximum between these two values. Historical June extremes in Wellington rarely exceed 18°C without strong subtropical advection, keeping higher outcomes at low implied probability. Updated official guidance from MetService or NIWA in the next 24–48 hours will provide the final resolution data.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 15 Jun '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction models from agencies including the Pakistan Meteorological Department indicate a daily maximum near the long-term June average of 34–36 °C for coastal Karachi on 15 June, driven by steady Arabian Sea breezes that limit daytime heating despite regional pre-monsoon warmth. These flows, combined with moderate humidity and limited cloud cover in current analyses, keep the highest temperature clustered around 34–35 °C in the market, with small divergences among ensemble members arising from slight differences in boundary-layer mixing and wind speed. No significant synoptic disturbance or heat-wave setup is forecast before mid-week, though traders monitor the next 48-hour model runs for any shift in sea-breeze strength that could tip the outcome by 1 °C.
